title: Deep sleep isn't empty
hookLine: Indra feared deep sleep was a blank; the Mandukya calls it gathered
carry: in deep sleep, the self is gathered, not gone
tomorrow: waking, dreaming, deep sleep. is there anything left after those?

cards: You've met Indra, king of the gods, living as Prajapati's student to learn the self. In the Chandogya, one answer he's given is the one in dreamless sleep. Indra walks away, then stops on the road.
In deep sleep, he says, a person doesn't even know 'I am this.' It's as if he's gone to nothing. So he goes back. Where are you, in the part of the night you never remember?
The Mandukya stops right at that gap.

teach.b: The Mandukya walks through the quarters of this self in order. Waking, which knows outward. Dreaming, which knows inward.
Then the third. In paraphrase: where the sleeper wants no wanting and sees no dream, that is deep sleep. The one there has become one, a mass of knowing, made of bliss, enjoying bliss.
Its name is prajna, the knowing one. Notice what the text refuses to say.
It doesn't call deep sleep empty. It calls it gathered: everything folded into one, nothing wanted, nothing seen apart.

Then it adds titles: the lord of all, the knower of all, the inner controller, the source where beings arise and come to rest. Advaita teachers point to the morning: you wake and say, i slept well, i knew nothing.
Someone was there to have slept well. For them, that's a clue the self doesn't switch off when the mind does. A neighbor tradition sings about the same stretch of night.

teach.h: THE PSALM: LAY ME DOWN IN PEACE.
teach.b: A psalm in the Hebrew Bible, in the King James Version, says: "I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety."
Here's what they share: sleep as a letting go, a peace nobody has to earn. And the honest difference.

teach.h: KEPT BY A THOU, OR FOUND AS THE SELF.
teach.b: The psalmist lies down trusting the LORD, a thou who keeps the sleeper safe. The Mandukya says the gathered sleeper is this self, the one it has just called Brahman.
Two old voices, each keeping watch over the quiet part of the night in its own words.

how: In Vedanta study, the Mandukya's quarters of the self (waking, dreaming, deep sleep, and the fourth) are read with Gaudapada's verses. Psalm 4 is part of the Hebrew Bible, read by Jews and Christians.

o: the self disappears each night in deep sleep
this self, even in deep sleep, is Brahman
the dreams you have are messages from God

games.q: the night, and a neighbor. tap the pairs.
p: a mass of knowing, made of bliss
lay me down in peace, and sleep

s: deep sleep is just dreaming that you forget
the Mandukya sets them apart: dreaming knows inward; in deep sleep the sleeper sees no dream.
right after deep sleep, the Mandukya names the inner controller
the lord of all, the knower of all, the inner controller, the source of all.

games.q: a friend says dreamless sleep is just a blank, like a phone switched off. how does the Mandukya describe it?
o: gathered: become one, a mass of knowing, made of bliss.
a blank: nothing at all is there until the morning.
a trip away from the self that ends when you wake.
games.why: where the sleeper wants no wanting and sees no dream: become one, a mass of knowing, made of bliss. and it calls this the lord of all.

practice: Close your eyes and let the body grow heavy, the way it does just before sleep, but stay awake. Let thoughts thin out without chasing them, and let wanting rest for a while. Notice the quiet that's left: not empty, just gathered.

wordCard.voice: Ayam atma brahma: this self, even in dreamless sleep, is a mass of knowing, and the Mandukya calls it the lord of all.

orig.note: Sanskrit: prajna, the knowing one, the Mandukya's name for this self in deep sleep.

carryVoice: Keep this one: in deep sleep, the self is gathered, not gone. Sleep well tonight.

sources.ref: Chandogya Upanishad 8.11.1–3 (Prajapati names the one in dreamless sleep as the self; Indra, on his way back, objects that then one does not know oneself as 'I am this', as if gone to destruction, and returns to study five more years)

Mandukya Upanishad 3–5 (waking, knowing outward; dreaming, knowing inward; deep sleep, where the sleeper desires no desire and sees no dream: become one, a mass of knowing, made of bliss, enjoying bliss, prajna)
Mandukya Upanishad 6 (this is the lord of all, the knower of all, the inner controller, the source of all, the arising and passing away of beings)
